headline_marked: [[SpaceX's record IPO]] sets stage for OpenAI and Anthropic public debuts.
headline: SpaceX's record IPO sets stage for OpenAI and Anthropic public debuts.
summary: SpaceX's massive public offering has analysts predicting a 'hot IPO summer,' with AI giants like OpenAI and Anthropic reportedly preparing to follow suit.
details: SpaceX recently completed the largest IPO ever, making CEO Elon Musk the world's first trillionaire. Despite its name, the company is emphasizing the potential of its costly AI business, a trend other AI firms may follow.

This move signals a potential 'hot IPO summer,' with competitors like OpenAI and Anthropic reportedly preparing for their own public market debuts. Analysts are discussing the implications of this new wave of tech IPOs.
SpaceX's IPO is seen as a 'stress test' for public markets, particularly regarding how much control a single person can exert over a public company. Other tech firms may try to emulate this model.

The market is experiencing a 'ripple effect,' with startups raising money for concepts like orbital data centers, a field popularized by SpaceX. This broader impact extends beyond just the headline-grabbing IPO.

This shift marks a change from the 'FAANG' era (Facebook, Amazon, Apple, Netflix, Google) to a new 'MANGOS' era, including Meta, Anthropic, NVIDIA, Google, OpenAI, and SpaceX. It highlights a move away from consumer/social networks towards AI labs and deep tech.
The anticipation for these IPOs means a busy period for reporters, with hundreds of pages of SEC filings expected. It signifies the reopening of the IPO market after years of private market focus.

A key question is whether Anthropic and OpenAI will try to emulate SpaceX's IPO strategy, which combines extreme aspects of early Google/Meta IPOs with Amazon's 'lose money forever' approach. The timing of these debuts is also a critical factor.

headline_marked: [[Google Pixel Call Screen blocks spam]] effectively, letting real calls through in a week-long test
headline: Google Pixel Call Screen blocks spam effectively, letting real calls through in a week-long test
summary: A user tested Google Pixel's Call Screen on "Maximum" protection for a week, finding it successfully blocked spam without deterring essential legitimate callers. The feature also includes on-device call transcription with Gemini Nano.
details: Spam calls are a growing nuisance, especially with the rise of robocallers. Google Pixel's Call Screen feature offers a solution, with three protection levels: Basic, Medium, and Maximum. The "Maximum" setting was put to the test for a week.

Maximum protection declines known spam and screens every call not in your contacts. Callers hear a prompt asking for their name and reason for calling, effectively defeating robocallers and most scam calls before the phone even rings.

The initial results were promising: the feature quickly declined confirmed spam numbers and cut off robocallers. Many spammers hung up immediately, with no ringing or missed-call notifications for the user.

A primary concern was whether this aggressive screening would deter legitimate first-time callers. However, most professionals complied with the prompt within seconds, and the tester reported not missing any expected appointments or business calls.

While effective for the tester, the "Maximum" setting might not suit everyone, particularly those whose jobs rely on cold calls from unsaved numbers. The feature also includes Call Notes, which uses Gemini Nano for on-device call transcription and summaries.

Call Notes provides an audible notification that recording has started and processes everything locally, addressing privacy concerns. Users can set auto-delete windows for recordings, though manual activation for every call is currently required.
